# Kite: agent documentation bundle

Current supported public APIs; roadmap features are not available. This bundle is generated with the guides and types. Consult the linked site for updates.

# How Kite works

Kite turns a small script into a native iPhone widget. You describe what to show,
where to place it, and what should happen when someone taps a button. Kite handles
turning that description into the widget you see on screen.

You can start from an example and change its words, colors and settings. You don't
need to build an iPhone app or connect your phone to a computer.

## From an idea to a widget

1. **Choose a starting point.** In Kite, create a Widget or Interactive widget.
   Give it a name, or keep the suggested one.
2. **Describe your content.** A script can show text, photos, progress, dates and
   data from a service. Its layout uses building blocks: a vertical stack puts
   items underneath each other; a horizontal stack puts them side by side.
3. **Try it in Kite.** Tap Run to see a preview. Change the layout or settings and
   Run again until it looks right. Errors and logs help you find problems.
4. **Add it to your Home Screen.** Add the Kite Script widget, choose a size, then
   select your script in Edit Widget. Each widget can have its own settings.
5. **Let iOS update it.** Kite prepares the content when the system requests an
   update. A refresh preference asks for updates; iOS chooses the actual timing.

[Create your first widget](https://juanbeniteza.github.io/kite-docs/Getting-started.html) walks through all five steps with
code you can copy. [Example scripts](https://juanbeniteza.github.io/kite-docs/index.html) give you a head start.

## What is inside a script?

Think of a script as a recipe with three parts:

- **Its label:** the name, supported sizes and options such as a message or a goal.
  In code, this is called `config`.
- **Its layout:** instructions for drawing the widget. For example, “show a title,
  a progress bar, and an Add button.” In code, this is `widget()`.
- **Its actions:** instructions to run after a tap, such as saving another glass
  of water. These are separate functions connected to the buttons.

Text that looks like `widget()` is a name used in code. A name on its own isn't a
complete script. The tutorials show complete files; the API reference describes
individual pieces you can use inside those files.

## Where do the numbers and images come from?

A widget can use text you enter in settings, data saved by a button, information
you allow it to read on your phone, or a request to an online service. Access to
things like Calendar needs your permission. Some services also need an API key;
keep keys in Kite's secrets settings, not in a file you share.

Kite starts a fresh run each time it needs to prepare content. To remember a
counter or completed habit, the script saves it in storage. A temporary variable
alone won't remember its value the next time the widget runs.

## Why doesn't everything update instantly?

A Home Screen widget isn't an app that runs continuously. iOS gives it short
opportunities to prepare its display so it can preserve battery life. It may show
saved content between updates. The preview is the quickest place to test edits.

Native countdown text can keep counting on screen without rerunning the script
every second. Buttons can run a short action and request updated content. Neither
mechanism makes a script a continuously running background process.

## More than Home Screen widgets

The same script can also provide a small Lock Screen view, an action that receives
input from Shortcuts, or a switch/button in Control Center. Those surfaces have
different sizes and behaviors, so test each one you plan to use. A script does not
add itself to any of these places automatically.

## Can an AI agent write the script?

Yes. Give your agent the [agent guide](https://juanbeniteza.github.io/kite-docs/Agent-guide.html) and describe what you want
it to show, which sizes you need, and where its data should come from. The guide
lists Kite's supported APIs and limits so the agent doesn't assume it is building
a web page. Review generated code before running it, especially if it uses private
data or online services. You can then paste its complete `.tsx` file into Kite.


---

# Point your agent here

Use this guide when asking an AI coding agent to create a Kite script. No access
to the private app repository is needed. The documentation describes the current
implementation; roadmap ideas are not available APIs.

## Give your agent this instruction

Copy this instruction and append your widget idea:

```text
Read https://juanbeniteza.github.io/kite-docs/llms-full.txt before writing code.
Create a Kite script using only the documented APIs and runtime capabilities.
Return one complete .tsx file, including config, imports and exported entry points.
Explain required permissions/secrets, supported sizes, installation and test steps.
State limitations honestly; do not invent APIs or promise exact background refreshes.
My idea: ...
```

If the agent cannot open URLs, download the plain-text guide and attach it to the
conversation. A link does not automatically give every agent browsing capability.

## Read these sources

- [How Kite works](https://juanbeniteza.github.io/kite-docs/How-Kite-works.html): a plain-language explanation for the user.
- [API reference](https://juanbeniteza.github.io/kite-docs/API-reference.html): supported arguments, properties and return types.
- [Type declarations](https://juanbeniteza.github.io/kite-docs/types/index.d.ts): the exact public contract.
- [Scripting guide](https://juanbeniteza.github.io/kite-docs/Scripting-guide.html): entry points and native services.
- [Daily Intention tutorial](https://juanbeniteza.github.io/kite-docs/Progressive-tutorial.html): a complete interactive script.
- [Water Garden](https://juanbeniteza.github.io/kite-docs/examples/Water%20Garden.tsx): persisted widget actions.
- [Quiet Frame](https://juanbeniteza.github.io/kite-docs/examples/Quiet%20Frame.tsx): native cached image loading and fallback.
- [Focus Session](https://juanbeniteza.github.io/kite-docs/examples/Focus%20Session.tsx): timelines, timer and control.

## Execution and output contract

- Deliver a single self-contained `.tsx` file by default. JavaScript/JSX is also
  supported, but TypeScript with JSX is the easiest shared format for examples.
- Use imports from `kite` and `kite/ui`. JSX creates native widget nodes; it is not
  React, HTML, CSS or a browser page. No React state/hooks, DOM, Node filesystem,
  npm package runtime, browser `fetch`, `setInterval`, or dynamic `eval`/`Function`.
  Use `http` for requests. Do not invent browser APIs from habit.
- Export `config = defineScript({...})` with a literal object. Metadata is parsed
  without executing the script. No computed fields, helper calls, spreads or
  variables inside config. Dynamic logic belongs in exported functions/helpers.
- `widget(ctx)` returns a Widget root or ascending `{ date, view }` timeline entries.
  `run()` handles app-only work/logging. `shortcut(input)` returns action output.
  `control` supplies button `press()` or toggle `get()`/`set(on)`.
- Every run starts with fresh JavaScript state. Persist JSON with `storage` and
  use `storage.update` for concurrent counters. Its callback can be retried: keep
  external side effects outside it. Dates should be saved as strings/timestamps.
- Buttons use `intent={exportedFunction}`, not a function call or inline closure.
  `params` is a JSON object passed to the handler. Widget Toggle adds `isOn` to
  that object: its handler receives `{ isOn, ...params }`. This differs from a
  Control Center toggle's `set(on)`, which receives a boolean directly.
- After a state change, return `{ reload: true }` and render the saved state again.
  Do not claim that changing a local variable updates a widget.

## Layout and system limits

- Use only the components/properties in the type declarations. Supported content
  includes stacks, grids, Text, Image, DateText, Gauge, ProgressView, Chart, Button,
  Toggle, Link, Spacer and Divider. No arbitrary HTML tags, CSS classes, web fonts,
  pixel font sizes or gradients unless an API explicitly documents them.
- Use named fonts and point-based frames. Keep layouts compact and check every
  declared family. Home Screen: small/medium/large, plus iPad extraLarge. Lock
  Screen: accessoryInline/accessoryCircular/accessoryRectangular with system
  tinting and restricted space. Don't promise a full-color Home Screen design on
  an accessory surface. Do not promise buttons in every accessory family.
- `ctx.date` is the rendering date; `ctx.displaySize` is in points, not pixels.
  Use `DateText` rather than importing `Date` and shadowing JavaScript's Date.
- iOS schedules widget runs. `refresh` is a hint, not a guaranteed interval.
  Timelines schedule display entries; they don't execute arbitrary code later.
  A native timer doesn't itself schedule notifications or trigger an action at zero.
- Keep work brief. The current normal deadline is 10 seconds with cooperative
  checks; native calls/engine built-ins aren't always interruptible. Don't add
  background loops or claim a measured memory budget that isn't documented.
- Phone compilation strips TS/JSX; it does not perform full TypeScript checking.
  Validate settings, missing storage and remote JSON at runtime. Gracefully handle
  permission denial, network failures and empty datasets.

## Native access and data

- Declare only needed permissions: network, files, calendar, reminders, location,
  notifications. Run in the app first for any required system prompts. Extensions
  cannot prompt for access. Declaration alone doesn't grant authorization.
- `storage`, `secrets`, `device` and `log` need no config permission. Secrets are
  per-script Keychain values: use `secrets.get`, not hardcoded tokens or logs.
- Use `http.image` for photos, then its returned source in Image. Native decoding
  downsizes the image; use caching and a useful offline view. Don't implement
  full-resolution image processing in JS.
- Use Kite's files API within its roots. Local files are shared with widget runs;
  iCloud file access is app-only. Do not assume arbitrary device filesystem access.
- Widget editor settings currently have four generic slots. App script settings
  expose the fuller configuration. Don't promise dynamically generated unlimited
  named system parameters or automatic placement of widgets/controls.
- Scriptable compatibility and Mac CLI/sync are roadmap work. Don't generate
  Scriptable globals, ListWidget or CLI commands as though already supported.
- Kite is for trusted scripts, not a sandbox for hostile source. Explain external
  service calls and sensitive data use. Don't embed credentials in shared output.

## Agent handoff checklist

Before handing over a script, check imports, literal config, complete exported
entry points, family layouts, persistent state, exported interaction references,
permissions and failure fallbacks. Separate APIs you verified from assumptions.
If a service contract is unknown, ask for it or clearly mark a placeholder URL;
never fabricate a working endpoint or claim testing you haven't performed.

Return installation steps: create a script, paste the complete file, Run in Kite,
configure any settings/secrets, check Preview/Logs, then add and configure Kite
Script, the Shortcuts action or the matching Kite control. Include expected output
and a repeatable tap/run test. Label preview/compiler checks separately from
physical-device checks. Don't require reinstalling the app for a script edit.

# Scripting guide

[Start with a complete first widget](https://juanbeniteza.github.io/kite-docs/Getting-started.html) if you're new to Kite.
Each code block below is a separate, complete script unless described otherwise.

## How a script runs

Kite calls exported entry points for the surface you're using:

| Export | Called for | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `widget(ctx)` | Widget rendering and preview | A `Widget` tree or dated timeline entries |
| `run()` | App execution for a run-only script | Work and console output |
| `shortcut(input)` | A Shortcuts action | Text, JSON, number or a supported file result |
| `control` | Control Center button or switch | `press()`, or `get()` and `set(on)` |
| Other exported functions | Widget Button/Toggle handlers | Usually `{ reload: true }` |

Run in the editor builds the script and tests its available surface; a control's
Preview has Press or switch controls. Defining a function doesn't execute its body.
For example, Focus Session starts when you press Start, not simply when you open it.

Each execution gets a fresh JavaScript context. A normal variable doesn't persist
between executions. Use `storage` for saved state shared by the same script's
app, widget and control runs. Different scripts have separate storage.

## Save data and add a button

This counter is a complete interactive widget. Tap **Add** in Preview or on the
Home Screen; the number should survive another Run.

```tsx
import { storage } from "kite";
import { Widget, VStack, Text, Button } from "kite/ui";

export const config = defineScript({
  name: "My Counter",
  widget: { families: ["small", "medium"], refresh: "daily" },
});

export async function increment() {
  await storage.update<number>("count", old => (old ?? 0) + 1);
  return { reload: true };
}

export async function widget() {
  const count = await storage.get<number>("count") ?? 0;
  return <Widget><VStack spacing={8}>
    <Text font="largeTitle" weight="bold">{count}</Text>
    <Button intent={increment} label="Add" symbol="plus.circle.fill" />
  </VStack></Widget>;
}
```

Use the exported function reference `intent={increment}`, not `increment()`.
The latter would call it while building the view. For parameters, pass a JSON
object through the Button's `params` property and accept it in your handler.
Prefer `storage.update` for counters so simultaneous actions don't overwrite
one another. `get`, `set`, `remove` and `keys` are also available. Store JSON values,
not functions or Date objects; store a date as an ISO string or timestamp.

## Layout and size

`Widget` contains `VStack`, `HStack` and `ZStack` containers. Use `Spacer`, `Divider`,
`Text`, `Image`, `DateText`, `Gauge`, `ProgressView`, `Chart`, `Button`, `Toggle`
and `Link` inside them. These render as native SwiftUI; CSS and HTML aren't supported.

Common properties include `padding`, `background`, `cornerRadius`, `opacity` and
`frame`. Text supports named fonts such as `headline`, `caption` and `largeTitle`,
plus `weight`, `color` and `lineLimit`. Sizes are in points.

Use `ctx.family` to show less content in `small` than in `large`. Home Screen
families are `small`, `medium`, `large` and iPad `extraLarge`. Lock Screen families
are `accessoryInline`, `accessoryCircular` and `accessoryRectangular`. Keep accessory
layouts simple: they use system tinting and have very little space. Choose a
supported family in `config.widget.families` and check it in Preview.

See [Daylight](https://juanbeniteza.github.io/kite-docs/examples/Daylight.tsx) for responsive layouts and progress.

## Settings and secrets

Declare settings as literal objects in `config.settings`, then read values through
`ctx.settings` in `widget`. Types are `text`, `number`, `toggle`, `enum`, `color` and
`secret`. Use defaults and validate values before calculations. The first-widget
tutorial demonstrates a text setting.

The current Home Screen widget editor has four generic setting slots. It can't
create unlimited named system fields from your source. Use Kite's script settings
for the full editor. Secret values belong in the app's secrets settings/Keychain;
read them with `await secrets.get("apiKey")` from `kite`. Don't hardcode keys in
source or log them.

`config` cannot depend on variables, function calls, spread expressions or computed
values. For instance, put `"My Widget"` directly in `config.name`, rather than a
variable containing that string. Ordinary dynamic logic belongs in functions.

## Network requests and photos

Declare `permissions: ["network"]` in `config`. Import `http` from `kite`.
`await http.json(url, { cache: "15m" })` downloads parsed JSON. With
`http.fetch`, check `response.ok` before reading `response.json()` or `text()`.
Handle errors and missing response fields so the widget still has useful content.

For images, use `await http.image(url, { cache: "1d" })`, then put the returned
source into `<Image src={source} />`. Kite downsizes images natively; don't download
full images as raw data just to resize them in JavaScript. `maxPixelSize` optionally
sets the longest edge in pixels.

[Quiet Frame](https://juanbeniteza.github.io/kite-docs/examples/Quiet%20Frame.tsx) is a complete downloadable photo widget
with a fallback. It needs internet access on the first load, but no API key.

## Permissions and native services

| Module imported from `kite` | Permission in `config.permissions` | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `http` | `network` | Requests, JSON and cached images |
| `files` | `files` | Read/write text files |
| `calendar` | `calendar` | Read calendars and create events |
| `reminders` | `reminders` | Read, create and complete reminders |
| `location` | `location` | Coordinates and geocoding |
| `notify` | `notifications` | Schedule/cancel notifications |
| `storage`, `secrets`, `device`, `log` | No declared permission | Saved JSON, Keychain, device info and logging |

Run permission-using scripts in Kite first. Only the app can present system
permission dialogs. A declaration alone doesn't grant system access. Keep background
work brief and handle denied access. iCloud file access is app-only; local script
files use shared storage available to widgets. Never assume arbitrary filesystem
access. See [the declarations](https://juanbeniteza.github.io/kite-docs/types/index.d.ts) for each method's arguments.

## Shortcuts

Create a **Shortcuts action** starter, or paste this script:

```tsx
export const config = defineScript({ name: "Uppercase Text" });

export async function shortcut(input: unknown) {
  const text = input == null ? "" : String(input);
  return text.toUpperCase();
}
```

Run it in Kite first. In Apple's Shortcuts app, create a shortcut, search for Kite,
add its run-script action, select **Uppercase Text**, and supply text as the input.
Add Show Result after it. With input `hello`, the result should be `HELLO`.
Kite provides separate actions for general text/JSON, number and file results;
choose the one matching your return value. This example uses text/JSON. Device
validation of the full Shortcuts UI flow is still pending.

## Control Center

This is a complete persisted switch. It doesn't require a widget:

```tsx
import { storage } from "kite";
import type { Control } from "kite";

export const config = defineScript({ name: "My Switch" });

export const control: Control = {
  kind: "toggle",
  title: "My Switch",
  symbol: "bolt.fill",
  async get() { return await storage.get<boolean>("on") ?? false; },
  async set(on: boolean) {
    await storage.set("on", on);
    return { reload: true };
  },
};
```

Run it and test the switch in Preview. Then edit Control Center, add **Kite Toggle**,
and choose **My Switch** in its configuration. It saves a boolean; it doesn't
operate a light or device until you add that integration yourself.

For a momentary action, use `kind: "button"` with `async press()` and add
**Kite Button** instead. [Focus Session](https://juanbeniteza.github.io/kite-docs/examples/Focus%20Session.tsx) combines a
button control, widget and shared storage in one script.

## Dates, countdowns and refreshes

Use `ctx.date` as the rendering date. `DateText` with `style="timer"` displays a
native relative timer; it doesn't require rerunning your script every second.
Return an array of `{ date, view }` entries to schedule different views for future
times, in ascending order. Daylight and Focus Session demonstrate this.

`refresh` hints include `"15m"`, `"30m"`, `"hourly"`, `"daily"` and `"never"`.
iOS controls actual widget execution. Don't use a JavaScript loop or `setInterval`
to keep a widget alive. Timers don't extend Kite's run deadline, and a displayed
countdown alone doesn't schedule a notification or execute a function when it ends.

## Runtime boundaries

Use `kite` modules rather than browser or Node APIs: there is no DOM, React runtime,
Node filesystem or Node package loader. TypeScript annotations are stripped on the
phone; the phone doesn't perform a full TypeScript typecheck. Dynamic code such as
`eval` and `new Function` is blocked. Deadline checks are cooperative; Kite is not a
security sandbox for hostile source. Read scripts before importing them.

To debug, add `console.log("count", count)`, Run, and open Logs. Avoid logging secrets
or personal data. Keep functions small and test changes in Preview before checking
the system widget. Share the `.tsx` file, with keys removed, through Files or a link.


---

# Build a daily intention widget

This tutorial builds one widget in five checkpoints. Start in Scripts → + → New
script → Widget. Name it Daily Intention. Replace its source with the complete file
at the end of this page, then explore each checkpoint. In the in-app guide,
**Create script from example** installs a separate editable copy.

## 1. Layout: make something visible

The final file uses a Widget with a vertical stack. The first Text is a heading;
the second displays your intention. Find `background="#172B28"` and change it to
`"#1B1530"`. Run and select small, then medium in Preview.

Expected: the same content fits both sizes and the background changes. Font names
are semantic sizes, not CSS. Keep enough contrast between text and background.

## 2. Settings: make it personal

`config.settings.intention` creates a text preference. The function reads it from
`ctx.settings.intention`. Open the script's settings in Kite and enter one small
goal. Run again.

Expected: the goal replaces “Take a short walk.” without editing code. In a real
Home Screen widget, configure that widget's settings separately. App preview
settings and system widget settings are different configurations.

## 3. Saved data: remember completion

`storage.get` loads a saved boolean. The `dayKey()` helper includes the local
calendar date, so completing today's intention doesn't mark tomorrow complete.
This file reads state only when rendered; iOS decides when the next render happens.

Run several times. Expected: Run alone doesn't mark anything complete. A module
variable would disappear between executions; storage persists for this script.

## 4. Interaction: do the work on tap

`complete()` is exported so the button can invoke it in a later execution. It saves
true, then asks for a reload. Tap Done in Preview, then Run again.

Expected: the message says Completed today. Repeated taps are safe. To try again
today, change the storage key prefix to `intention-test-` in both functions (the
shared `dayKey()` helper already handles this), or create a new copy of the script.

## 5. Home Screen: test outside the app

Run once in Kite. Add a small or medium Kite Script widget and choose Daily
Intention. Set the intention for that widget, then tap Done on the Home Screen.

Expected: the button records completion without opening an editor. If Preview
works but the Home Screen doesn't, use Troubleshooting before changing the code.
Do not treat refresh hints as exact timers.

## Complete script

```tsx
import { storage } from "kite";
import type { WidgetContext } from "kite";
import { Widget, VStack, Text, Button } from "kite/ui";

export const config = defineScript({
  name: "Daily Intention",
  icon: { symbol: "leaf.fill", color: "#72DCC5" },
  widget: { families: ["small", "medium"], refresh: "hourly" },
  settings: {
    intention: { type: "text", title: "Intention", default: "Take a short walk." },
  },
});

function dayKey() {
  const date = new Date();
  return `intention-${date.getFullYear()}-${date.getMonth() + 1}-${date.getDate()}`;
}

export async function complete() {
  await storage.set(dayKey(), true);
  return { reload: true };
}

export async function widget(ctx: WidgetContext) {
  const done = await storage.get<boolean>(dayKey()) ?? false;
  return <Widget background="#172B28"><VStack align="leading" spacing={8}>
    <Text font="caption" weight="bold" color="#72DCC5">TODAY'S INTENTION</Text>
    <Text font="headline" color="#FFFFFF" lineLimit={3}>
      {String(ctx.settings.intention ?? "Take a short walk.")}
    </Text>
    {done
      ? <Text font="caption" color="#72DCC5">Completed today</Text>
      : <Button intent={complete} label="Done" symbol="checkmark.circle.fill" />}
  </VStack></Widget>;
}
```

Next experiments: add a reset handler, display a second line only for medium, or
replace the text setting with an enum of goals. Keep config values literal and
export every interaction handler. See API reference for exact properties.


---

# API reference

Generated from the current public declarations. `?` means optional; `Promise<T>`
means await the result. Import values from the module heading. Type annotations
help your editor, but the phone strips them rather than checking them.

Defaults are stated where guaranteed by declarations. Other optional rendering
properties use native renderer/system behavior; specify them when appearance matters.
All component functions return a widget node. No CSS or React runtime is involved.

# Globals

`console.log()` writes messages to Kite’s Logs. `setTimeout()` schedules a short callback during the current run; `clearTimeout()` cancels it. These are API names, not complete scripts. Timers do not extend the run deadline. `defineScript()` declares literal script metadata and is available without importing it. JSX types describe Kite widget nodes, not HTML.

# Module kite

## Family

See the signature for supported fields, optional values and return types.

```ts
export type Family = "small" | "medium" | "large" | "extraLarge" | "accessoryCircular" | "accessoryRectangular" | "accessoryInline";
```

## JSONValue

See the signature for supported fields, optional values and return types.

```ts
export type JSONValue = string | number | boolean | null | JSONValue[] | { [key: string]: JSONValue };
```

## Surface

See the signature for supported fields, optional values and return types.

```ts
export type Surface = "app" | "widget" | "intent" | "control" | "shortcut";
```

## Permission

See the signature for supported fields, optional values and return types.

```ts
export type Permission = "network" | "files" | "calendar" | "reminders" | "location" | "notifications";
```

## SettingDeclaration

See the signature for supported fields, optional values and return types.

```ts
export type SettingDeclaration =
  | { type: "enum"; options: readonly string[]; default?: string; title?: string }
  | { type: "text"; default?: string; title?: string; placeholder?: string }
  | { type: "number"; default?: number; min?: number; max?: number; title?: string }
  | { type: "toggle"; default?: boolean; title?: string }
  | { type: "color"; default?: string; title?: string }
  | { type: "secret"; title?: string };
```

## ScriptConfig

See the signature for supported fields, optional values and return types.

```ts
export interface ScriptConfig {
  name?: string;
  description?: string;
  icon?: { symbol: string; color?: string };
  widget?: {
    families?: readonly Family[];
    /** A hint for the next timeline request. iOS decides when widgets actually refresh. */
    refresh?: "never" | "15m" | "30m" | "hourly" | "daily" | number;
  };
  /** Shown natively when the user edits the widget. Secrets live in the Keychain. */
  settings?: Record<string, SettingDeclaration>;
  permissions?: readonly Permission[];
}
```

## SettingValues

See the signature for supported fields, optional values and return types.

```ts
export type SettingValues = Record<string, string | number | boolean | undefined> & { parameter?: string };
```

## WidgetContext

See the signature for supported fields, optional values and return types.

```ts
export interface WidgetContext {
  family: Family;
  settings: SettingValues;
  surface: Surface;
  /** ISO 8601 time of this run. */
  date: string;
  /** Point size of the widget, when known. */
  displaySize: { width: number; height: number };
  scriptId: string;
}
```

## TimelineEntry

See the signature for supported fields, optional values and return types.

```ts
export interface TimelineEntry { date: Date | string | number; view: import("kite/ui").WidgetNode; }
```

## WidgetResult

See the signature for supported fields, optional values and return types.

```ts
export type WidgetResult = import("kite/ui").WidgetNode | TimelineEntry[];
```

## IntentResult

See the signature for supported fields, optional values and return types.

```ts
export interface IntentResult { reload?: boolean }
```

## ControlToggle

See the signature for supported fields, optional values and return types.

```ts
export interface ControlToggle { kind: "toggle"; title?: string; symbol?: string; get(): boolean | Promise<boolean>; set(on: boolean): void | IntentResult | Promise<void | IntentResult>; }
```

## ControlButton

See the signature for supported fields, optional values and return types.

```ts
export interface ControlButton { kind: "button"; title?: string; symbol?: string; press(): void | IntentResult | Promise<void | IntentResult>; }
```

## Control

See the signature for supported fields, optional values and return types.

```ts
export type Control = ControlToggle | ControlButton;
```

## defineScript

See the signature for supported fields, optional values and return types.

```ts
export function defineScript<const C extends ScriptConfig>(config: C): C;
```

## RequestOptions

See the signature for supported fields, optional values and return types.

```ts
export interface RequestOptions {
  method?: "GET" | "POST" | "PUT" | "PATCH" | "DELETE" | "HEAD";
  headers?: Record<string, string>;
  body?: string;
  /** Serve from Kite's shared cache when fresher than this, e.g. "30s", "15m", "1h", "1d". */
  cache?: string;
  /** Seconds, default 15, max 30. */
  timeout?: number;
}
```

## Response

See the signature for supported fields, optional values and return types.

```ts
export interface Response {
  readonly status: number;
  readonly ok: boolean;
  readonly headers: Record<string, string>;
  readonly url: string;
  readonly fromCache: boolean;
  readonly body: string;
  text(): Promise<string>;
  json<T = any>(): Promise<T>;
}
```

## ImageOptions

See the signature for supported fields, optional values and return types.

```ts
export interface ImageOptions extends Pick<RequestOptions, "headers" | "cache" | "timeout"> {
  /** Longest edge in pixels. Defaults to the widget's pixel size. Images are downscaled natively. */
  maxPixelSize?: number;
}
```

## http

Requires network. Cache windows are strings such as "15m". Handle failed requests. Request timeout is in seconds (default 15, maximum 30). image returns a cached image source; native downscaling defaults to the widget pixel size.

```ts
export const http: {
  fetch(url: string, options?: RequestOptions): Promise<Response>;
  json<T = any>(url: string, options?: RequestOptions): Promise<T>;
  /** Downloads and natively downscales an image. Returns a source for <Image src>. */
  image(url: string, options?: ImageOptions): Promise<string>;
};
```

## storage

Per-script JSON shared across surfaces. Missing keys return undefined. Use update for counters, since it retries concurrent changes; keep its callback free of external side effects.

```ts
export const storage: {
  get<T extends JSONValue = JSONValue>(key: string): Promise<T | undefined>;
  set(key: string, value: JSONValue): Promise<void>;
  update<T extends JSONValue = JSONValue>(key: string, fn: (value: T | undefined) => T | Promise<T>): Promise<T>;
  remove(key: string): Promise<void>;
  keys(): Promise<string[]>;
};
```

## secrets

Per-script Keychain values. Missing names return undefined. Configure keys in the app; never put them in a shared source file.

```ts
export const secrets: {
  get(name: string): Promise<string | undefined>;
  set(name: string, value: string): Promise<void>;
  remove(name: string): Promise<void>;
};
```

## FileOptions

See the signature for supported fields, optional values and return types.

```ts
export interface FileOptions {
  /** "local" (default, shared with widgets) or "icloud" (app only). */
  location?: "local" | "icloud";
}
```

## FileEntry

See the signature for supported fields, optional values and return types.

```ts
export interface FileEntry { name: string; path: string; isDirectory: boolean; size: number; modified: string }
```

## files

Requires files. Paths are relative to Kite file roots. Default location is local (shared with widgets); icloud is app-only. Text methods use strings, not arbitrary binary buffers.

```ts
export const files: {
  read(path: string, options?: FileOptions): Promise<string>;
  write(path: string, text: string, options?: FileOptions): Promise<void>;
  append(path: string, text: string, options?: FileOptions): Promise<void>;
  list(path?: string, options?: FileOptions): Promise<FileEntry[]>;
  exists(path: string, options?: FileOptions): Promise<boolean>;
  remove(path: string, options?: FileOptions): Promise<void>;
  /** Path prefix for a folder bookmarked in Kite's settings, e.g. "bookmark:Notes/". */
  bookmark(name: string): Promise<string>;
};
```

Requires location. Run in the app first for authorization; handle unavailable locations.

```ts
export const location: {
```

## notify

Requires notifications. schedule returns an id; keep it to cancel later. action is a URL opened when the notification is tapped.

```ts
export const notify: {
  /** Returns the notification id. `action` is a URL opened when the notification is tapped. */
  schedule(options: { title: string; body?: string; at?: Date | string; action?: string; id?: string }): Promise<string>;
  cancel(id: string): Promise<void>;
};
```

## device

No declared permission. battery level can be null; handle unknown battery state.

```ts
export const device: {
  readonly locale: string;
  readonly colorScheme: "light" | "dark";
  readonly screen: { width: number; height: number; scale: number };
  readonly model: string;
  readonly systemVersion: string;

};
```

## log

No declared permission. Logs appear in Kite; console.log/info/debug/warn/error are also available. Avoid private data.

```ts
export const log: {
  debug(...values: unknown[]): void;
  info(...values: unknown[]): void;
  warn(...values: unknown[]): void;
  error(...values: unknown[]): void;
};
```

# Module kite/ui

## WidgetNode

See the signature for supported fields, optional values and return types.

```ts
export interface WidgetNode {
  type: string;
  props?: Record<string, JSONValue>;
  children?: (WidgetNode | string)[];
}
type Child = WidgetNode | string | number | boolean | null | undefined | Child[];
type Color = string;
type Length = number | "infinity";
type Alignment = "center" | "leading" | "trailing" | "top" | "bottom" | "topLeading" | "topTrailing" | "bottomLeading" | "bottomTrailing";
type Font = "largeTitle" | "title" | "title2" | "title3" | "headline" | "subheadline" | "body" | "callout" | "footnote" | "caption" | "caption2";
type IntentFunction = (params: any) => unknown;
```

## Modifiers

See the signature for supported fields, optional values and return types.

```ts
export interface Modifiers {
  padding?: number | { top?: number; leading?: number; bottom?: number; trailing?: number; horizontal?: number; vertical?: number };
  frame?: { width?: number; height?: number; minWidth?: number; maxWidth?: Length; minHeight?: number; maxHeight?: Length; alignment?: Alignment };
  background?: Color;
  cornerRadius?: number;
  opacity?: number;
  foreground?: Color;
  widgetAccentable?: boolean;
  privacySensitive?: boolean;
}
interface Container extends Modifiers { children?: Child }
```

## Widget

Root of a widget tree. url sets its open destination. Backgrounds on Lock Screen accessories are controlled by the system.

```ts
export function Widget(props: Container & { url?: string; background?: Color; relevance?: number }): WidgetNode;
```

## VStack

Vertical layout. align controls horizontal alignment; spacing is in points.

```ts
export function VStack(props: Container & { align?: "leading" | "center" | "trailing"; spacing?: number }): WidgetNode;
```

## HStack

Horizontal layout. align controls vertical alignment; spacing is in points.

```ts
export function HStack(props: Container & { align?: "top" | "center" | "bottom"; spacing?: number }): WidgetNode;
```

## ZStack

Layers children back to front. align positions them within the stack.

```ts
export function ZStack(props: Container & { align?: Alignment }): WidgetNode;
```

## Grid

Contains GridRow children. hSpacing and vSpacing control gaps in points.

```ts
export function Grid(props: Container & { hSpacing?: number; vSpacing?: number; align?: Alignment }): WidgetNode;
```

## GridRow

One row of cells inside Grid.

```ts
export function GridRow(props: Container): WidgetNode;
```

## Text

children is the displayed content. Use named fonts and hex colors. lineLimit limits wrapping; minScale permits shrinking to fit.

```ts
export function Text(props: Modifiers & { font?: Font; color?: Color; weight?: "regular" | "medium" | "semibold" | "bold" | "heavy"; design?: "default" | "rounded" | "monospaced" | "serif"; lineLimit?: number; minScale?: number; align?: "leading" | "center" | "trailing"; children?: Child }): WidgetNode;
```

## Image

Use symbol for SF Symbols or src for a cached image source. aspect controls fit/fill. Set a frame when constraining a photo.

```ts
export function Image(props: Modifiers & { src?: string; symbol?: string; resizable?: boolean; aspect?: "fit" | "fill"; color?: Color; font?: Font }): WidgetNode;
```

## Date

Native date display. Prefer importing DateText to avoid shadowing JavaScript Date. timer updates without executing the script each second.

```ts
export function Date(props: Modifiers & { value: globalThis.Date | string | number; style?: "relative" | "timer" | "time" | "date" | "offset"; font?: Font; color?: Color }): WidgetNode;
```

## DateText

Alias of the Date component, recommended to preserve access to global Date.

```ts
export const DateText: typeof Date;
```

## Gauge

Value indicator. Supply range explicitly for a known scale and choose linear/circular style.

```ts
export function Gauge(props: Modifiers & { value: number; range?: [number, number]; label?: string; style?: "linear" | "circular"; color?: Color }): WidgetNode;
```

## ProgressView

Progress indicator. Supply value and total explicitly for a known scale.

```ts
export function ProgressView(props: Modifiers & { value: number; total?: number; label?: string; color?: Color }): WidgetNode;
```

## Chart

data is an array of records; x and y name fields. Set mark explicitly for line, bar or area.

```ts
export function Chart(props: Modifiers & { data: Record<string, JSONValue>[]; mark?: "line" | "bar" | "area" | "point"; x: string; y: string; color?: Color }): WidgetNode;
```

## Button

intent must reference an exported function. params are JSON data passed to it. Use label/symbol or child content.

```ts
export function Button(props: Modifiers & { intent: IntentFunction; params?: Record<string, JSONValue>; symbol?: string; label?: string; children?: Child }): WidgetNode;
```

## Toggle

isOn is the persisted value from your script; its exported intent receives the new state. Render from saved state again after the action.

```ts
export function Toggle(props: Modifiers & { isOn: boolean; intent: IntentFunction; params?: Record<string, JSONValue>; label?: string; symbol?: string; children?: Child }): WidgetNode;
```

## Link

Wrap content in a URL destination.

```ts
export function Link(props: Container & { url: string }): WidgetNode;
```

## Spacer

Flexible empty space; minLength sets a minimum in points.

```ts
export function Spacer(props?: Modifiers & { minLength?: number }): WidgetNode;
```

## Divider

Native separator between content.

```ts
export function Divider(props?: Modifiers): WidgetNode;
```

# Native module usage examples

These are fragments to use inside an async entry point. Import the named module
from kite and declare its permission as described above. URLs are placeholders;
supply your own endpoint and validate its response.

## http example

```ts
const data = await http.json("https://example.com/data.json", { cache: "15m" });
```

## storage example

```ts
await storage.update<number>("count", old => (old ?? 0) + 1);
```

## secrets example

```ts
const token = await secrets.get("apiKey");
```

## files example

```ts
await files.append("Notes.txt", "A note\n");
```

## calendar example

```ts
const events = await calendar.events({ from: new Date(), limit: 5 });
```

## reminders example

```ts
const tasks = await reminders.list({ completed: false });
```

## location example

```ts
const coordinates = await location.current({ accuracy: "kilometer" });
```

## notify example

```ts
const id = await notify.schedule({ title: "Take a break", at: new Date(Date.now() + 60000) });
```

## device example

```ts
const battery = await device.battery();
```

## log example

```ts
log.info("Widget rendered");
```

# Component examples

These JSX fragments go inside a widget return. Import their components from kite/ui.
Button and Toggle use a placeholder exported handler: implement its persisted
state changes in your script (see the interactive tutorial). For photos, use an
Image src returned by http.image rather than symbol. GridRow is demonstrated inside Grid.

```jsx
<Widget background="#172B28"><Text>Hello</Text></Widget>
```




## Text example

```jsx
<Text font="headline" weight="bold" color="#72DCC5" lineLimit={2}>Hello</Text>
```

## Image example

```jsx
<Image symbol="heart.fill" font="title" color="#FF6688" />
```

## DateText example

```jsx
<DateText value={new Date(Date.now() + 60000)} style="timer" font="title" />
```

## Gauge example

```jsx

```

## ProgressView example

```jsx
<ProgressView value={3} total={8} label="Water" color="#72DCC5" />
```

## Chart example

```jsx

```

## Button example

```jsx

```

## Toggle example


## Divider example

```jsx
<Divider />
```

# Shared layout types

These types explain the aliases used by component signatures. All components
accept Modifiers. Colors are strings such as hex values; lengths are points.

```ts
type Child = WidgetNode | string | number | boolean | null | undefined | Child[];
  type Color = string;
  type Length = number | "infinity";
  type Alignment = "center" | "leading" | "trailing" | "top" | "bottom" | "topLeading" | "topTrailing" | "bottomLeading" | "bottomTrailing";
  type Font = "largeTitle" | "title" | "title2" | "title3" | "headline" | "subheadline" | "body" | "callout" | "footnote" | "caption" | "caption2";
  type IntentFunction = (params: any) => unknown;

  /** Modifiers available on every component. */
  export interface Modifiers {
    padding?: number | { top?: number; leading?: number; bottom?: number; trailing?: number; horizontal?: number; vertical?: number };
    frame?: { width?: number; height?: number; minWidth?: number; maxWidth?: Length; minHeight?: number; maxHeight?: Length; alignment?: Alignment };
    background?: Color;
    cornerRadius?: number;
    opacity?: number;
    foreground?: Color;
    widgetAccentable?: boolean;
    privacySensitive?: boolean;
  }
  interface Container extends Modifiers { children?: Child }
```


---

# Troubleshooting

Use this order: save and Run in Kite → read the first error → check Preview → test
the actual widget, shortcut or control. Fix one thing at a time. Logs can contain
personal information; remove tokens and private data before sharing them.

## Compile errors

**Unexpected token / JSX parse error:** confirm the filename ends in `.tsx` or
`.jsx` when it contains tags. Check matching braces, parentheses, quotes and closing
tags. The reported position may follow the real mistake, so check the previous line.
Smart quotes pasted from prose can break JavaScript. Copy examples from code blocks.

**Invalid config / metadata error:** config is read without running source. Write
literal strings, numbers, booleans, arrays and plain objects. Don't compute a name,
spread another object into config, or call helpers there. Put logic in functions.

**Import/module/export error:** use supported `kite` and `kite/ui` imports. Node,
browser and arbitrary npm dependencies aren't available. Check spelling and export
`widget`, `shortcut`, `control` or `run`. Relative modules require their files to be
present in the library; start with one complete file when diagnosing imports.

## Runtime errors

**Undefined / cannot read property:** inspect the value before accessing a field.
A setting may be absent, storage may have no value, and a network response may not
match your assumed shape. Use defaults and validate untrusted JSON. Phone compilation
strips types; it doesn't prove that external data matches a TypeScript annotation.

**Timeout:** remove endless loops and unnecessary work. Cache requests and reduce
large inputs. Don't try to keep a script running to animate a widget. A deadline is
cooperative; it doesn't make every native call or engine built-in interruptible.

**Invalid result:** widget must return a Widget tree or dated entries containing
`date` and `view`. Don't return raw strings, Promises you forgot to await inside
data, or circular JavaScript objects. See the first-widget example.

## Requests and permissions

**Permission denied / undeclared permission:** add the relevant literal permission
in config, then Run in the app. Widgets and controls cannot present authorization
prompts. If you already denied system access, review Kite in iOS Settings. Return
safe fallback content when permission stays denied. Network declaration is required
but doesn't itself grant access to calendar, location or other protected data.

**HTTP failure:** check status with `http.fetch` and verify the URL, authentication,
service response and connectivity. Log a status or a redacted summary, not an API
key or the full private response. Cache can serve old content; shorten the cache
window while diagnosing, then restore a reasonable window. API keys belong in secrets.

**Photo blank:** load through `http.image`, pass the returned source to Image, and
provide an aspect and useful space in the layout. Run online in the app first.
Handle download failure with text or an SF Symbol. Don't assume a remote URL is a
local cached image source. Quiet Frame is a working reference.

## Widget problems

**Script absent:** Run in Kite and resolve compile errors first. Export widget and
declare the family you're adding. Pick Kite Script, not an internal benchmark widget.
Refresh the library after copying a file through Files.

**Preview works, Home Screen is stale or blank:** verify the widget's selected script
and setting slots, Run again in Kite, and wait for the system's reload. Refresh is a
hint. Preview and real widgets have different execution environments and budgets.
A prior failure can leave the last good render visible. Inspect logs/Diagnostics for
that surface before assuming your latest edit ran. Record the time, script, size,
iOS version and screenshot if the problem persists.

**Button does nothing:** pass an exported function reference to intent, not a call.
Save state with storage, return `{ reload: true }`, and render the state again.
A value held only in a module variable disappears after execution. Keep handler
parameters JSON-compatible. Test Preview and Home Screen separately.

**Lock Screen looks different:** accessory widgets use system tinting and small
layouts. Background colors and full Home Screen compositions won't transfer directly.
Test the exact accessory family and reduce content.

## Shortcuts and controls

**No shortcut output:** export shortcut(input), supply input in the Shortcuts action,
and choose the action matching text/JSON, number or file output. A console log isn't
the returned result. Check Preview output first, then Show Result in Shortcuts.

**Control missing:** export a control with kind toggle or button. Run in Kite, then
add the corresponding Kite Toggle or Kite Button and choose the script. Merely
exporting control doesn't add it to Control Center automatically.

**Control resets:** implement get() using persistent storage, and write the same
key in set(on). A control with a boolean variable at file scope loses it each run.

## Recovery without losing scripts

Copy the script file somewhere safe before large edits. Removing a Home Screen
widget doesn't fix source errors. Avoid reinstalling Kite as an initial debugging
step: local files and state may be lost. Keep a backup and use a fresh copy of the
smallest example to separate source problems from environment problems.

For a useful bug report include: the smallest script that reproduces it (secrets
removed), what you expected, what happened, family/surface, app build, iOS version,
and relevant redacted logs. Device benchmark CSV is useful for the three-day
reliability test, but isn't required for an ordinary syntax question.


---

# Exact public type declarations

```ts
// @kite/types — public declarations for Kite scripts.
// Every public JS API must be declared here and covered by a fixture.

/** Declares a script's static metadata. Kite reads it without running the script. */
declare function defineScript<const C extends import("kite").ScriptConfig>(config: C): C;

/** Script globals provided by Kite's runtime (no DOM or Node APIs). */
declare const console: {
  log(...values: unknown[]): void;
  info(...values: unknown[]): void;
  debug(...values: unknown[]): void;
  warn(...values: unknown[]): void;
  error(...values: unknown[]): void;
};
/** Timers run within the script's deadline; a pending timer does not extend it. */
declare function setTimeout(callback: (...args: any[]) => void, milliseconds?: number, ...args: any[]): number;
declare function clearTimeout(id: number | undefined): void;

declare namespace JSX {
  type Element = import("kite/ui").WidgetNode;
  interface ElementChildrenAttribute { children: {}; }
  interface IntrinsicAttributes { key?: string | number; }
}

declare module "kite" {
  export type Family = "small" | "medium" | "large" | "extraLarge" | "accessoryCircular" | "accessoryRectangular" | "accessoryInline";
  export type JSONValue = string | number | boolean | null | JSONValue[] | { [key: string]: JSONValue };
  export type Surface = "app" | "widget" | "intent" | "control" | "shortcut";
  export type Permission = "network" | "files" | "calendar" | "reminders" | "location" | "notifications";

  export type SettingDeclaration =
    | { type: "enum"; options: readonly string[]; default?: string; title?: string }
    | { type: "text"; default?: string; title?: string; placeholder?: string }
    | { type: "number"; default?: number; min?: number; max?: number; title?: string }
    | { type: "toggle"; default?: boolean; title?: string }
    | { type: "color"; default?: string; title?: string }
    | { type: "secret"; title?: string };

  export interface ScriptConfig {
    name?: string;
    description?: string;
    icon?: { symbol: string; color?: string };
    widget?: {
      families?: readonly Family[];
      /** A hint for the next timeline request. iOS decides when widgets actually refresh. */
      refresh?: "never" | "15m" | "30m" | "hourly" | "daily" | number;
    };
    /** Shown natively when the user edits the widget. Secrets live in the Keychain. */
    settings?: Record<string, SettingDeclaration>;
    permissions?: readonly Permission[];
  }

  export type SettingValues = Record<string, string | number | boolean | undefined> & { parameter?: string };

  export interface WidgetContext {
    family: Family;
    settings: SettingValues;
    surface: Surface;
    /** ISO 8601 time of this run. */
    date: string;
    /** Point size of the widget, when known. */
    displaySize: { width: number; height: number };
    scriptId: string;
  }

  export interface TimelineEntry { date: Date | string | number; view: import("kite/ui").WidgetNode; }
  export type WidgetResult = import("kite/ui").WidgetNode | TimelineEntry[];
  export interface IntentResult { reload?: boolean }

  export interface ControlToggle { kind: "toggle"; title?: string; symbol?: string; get(): boolean | Promise<boolean>; set(on: boolean): void | IntentResult | Promise<void | IntentResult>; }
  export interface ControlButton { kind: "button"; title?: string; symbol?: string; press(): void | IntentResult | Promise<void | IntentResult>; }
  export type Control = ControlToggle | ControlButton;

  export function defineScript<const C extends ScriptConfig>(config: C): C;

  // ---- http -----------------------------------------------------------------
  export interface RequestOptions {
    method?: "GET" | "POST" | "PUT" | "PATCH" | "DELETE" | "HEAD";
    headers?: Record<string, string>;
    body?: string;
    /** Serve from Kite's shared cache when fresher than this, e.g. "30s", "15m", "1h", "1d". */
    cache?: string;
    /** Seconds, default 15, max 30. */
    timeout?: number;
  }
  export interface Response {
    readonly status: number;
    readonly ok: boolean;
    readonly headers: Record<string, string>;
    readonly url: string;
    readonly fromCache: boolean;
    readonly body: string;
    text(): Promise<string>;
    json<T = any>(): Promise<T>;
  }
  export interface ImageOptions extends Pick<RequestOptions, "headers" | "cache" | "timeout"> {
    /** Longest edge in pixels. Defaults to the widget's pixel size. Images are downscaled natively. */
    maxPixelSize?: number;
  }
  export const http: {
    fetch(url: string, options?: RequestOptions): Promise<Response>;
    json<T = any>(url: string, options?: RequestOptions): Promise<T>;
    /** Downloads and natively downscales an image. Returns a source for <Image src>. */
    image(url: string, options?: ImageOptions): Promise<string>;
  };

  // ---- storage / secrets / files -------------------------------------------------
  /** JSON values shared by this script's app runs, widgets, intents and controls. */
  export const storage: {
    get<T extends JSONValue = JSONValue>(key: string): Promise<T | undefined>;
    set(key: string, value: JSONValue): Promise<void>;
    update<T extends JSONValue = JSONValue>(key: string, fn: (value: T | undefined) => T | Promise<T>): Promise<T>;
    remove(key: string): Promise<void>;
    keys(): Promise<string[]>;
  };
  /** Keychain items private to this script. */
  export const secrets: {
    get(name: string): Promise<string | undefined>;
    set(name: string, value: string): Promise<void>;
    remove(name: string): Promise<void>;
  };
  export interface FileOptions {
    /** "local" (default, shared with widgets) or "icloud" (app only). */
    location?: "local" | "icloud";
  }
  export interface FileEntry { name: string; path: string; isDirectory: boolean; size: number; modified: string }
  export const files: {
    read(path: string, options?: FileOptions): Promise<string>;
    write(path: string, text: string, options?: FileOptions): Promise<void>;
    append(path: string, text: string, options?: FileOptions): Promise<void>;
    list(path?: string, options?: FileOptions): Promise<FileEntry[]>;
    exists(path: string, options?: FileOptions): Promise<boolean>;
    remove(path: string, options?: FileOptions): Promise<void>;
    /** Path prefix for a folder bookmarked in Kite's settings, e.g. "bookmark:Notes/". */
    bookmark(name: string): Promise<string>;
  };

  // ---- calendar / reminders -------------------------------------------------------
  export interface CalendarInfo { id: string; title: string; color: string; allowsModifications: boolean }
  export interface CalendarEvent {
    id: string; title: string; start: Date; end: Date; isAllDay: boolean;
    location?: string; notes?: string; calendar: string; calendarColor: string;
  }
  export interface NewEvent { title: string; start: Date | string; end: Date | string; isAllDay?: boolean; location?: string; notes?: string; calendar?: string }
  export const calendar: {
    calendars(): Promise<CalendarInfo[]>;
    events(options?: { from?: Date | string; to?: Date | string; calendars?: string[]; limit?: number }): Promise<CalendarEvent[]>;
    createEvent(event: NewEvent): Promise<CalendarEvent>;
  };
  export interface Reminder { id: string; title: string; due?: Date; completed: boolean; completedAt?: Date; notes?: string; list: string; priority: number }
  export const reminders: {
    list(options?: { due?: Date | string; completed?: boolean; lists?: string[]; limit?: number }): Promise<Reminder[]>;
    create(reminder: { title: string; due?: Date | string; notes?: string; list?: string; priority?: number }): Promise<Reminder>;
    complete(id: string): Promise<void>;
  };

  // ---- location / notify / device / log -------------------------------------------
  export interface Coordinates { latitude: number; longitude: number; accuracy: number; altitude?: number; timestamp: Date }
  export interface Place { name?: string; locality?: string; region?: string; country?: string; postalCode?: string; latitude: number; longitude: number }
  export const location: {
    current(options?: { accuracy?: "best" | "tenMeters" | "hundredMeters" | "kilometer" | "threeKilometers" }): Promise<Coordinates>;
    geocode(query: string): Promise<Place[]>;
    reverse(latitude: number, longitude: number): Promise<Place[]>;
  };
  export const notify: {
    /** Returns the notification id. `action` is a URL opened when the notification is tapped. */
    schedule(options: { title: string; body?: string; at?: Date | string; action?: string; id?: string }): Promise<string>;
    cancel(id: string): Promise<void>;
  };
  export const device: {
    readonly locale: string;
    readonly colorScheme: "light" | "dark";
    readonly screen: { width: number; height: number; scale: number };
    readonly model: string;
    readonly systemVersion: string;
    battery(): Promise<{ level: number | null; state: "unknown" | "unplugged" | "charging" | "full" }>;
  };
  export const log: {
    debug(...values: unknown[]): void;
    info(...values: unknown[]): void;
    warn(...values: unknown[]): void;
    error(...values: unknown[]): void;
  };
}

declare module "kite/ui" {
  import type { JSONValue } from "kite";

  /** The JSON tree that JSX compiles to. No React runtime ships. */
  export interface WidgetNode {
    type: string;
    props?: Record<string, JSONValue>;
    children?: (WidgetNode | string)[];
  }
  type Child = WidgetNode | string | number | boolean | null | undefined | Child[];
  type Color = string;
  type Length = number | "infinity";
  type Alignment = "center" | "leading" | "trailing" | "top" | "bottom" | "topLeading" | "topTrailing" | "bottomLeading" | "bottomTrailing";
  type Font = "largeTitle" | "title" | "title2" | "title3" | "headline" | "subheadline" | "body" | "callout" | "footnote" | "caption" | "caption2";
  type IntentFunction = (params: any) => unknown;

  /** Modifiers available on every component. */
  export interface Modifiers {
    padding?: number | { top?: number; leading?: number; bottom?: number; trailing?: number; horizontal?: number; vertical?: number };
    frame?: { width?: number; height?: number; minWidth?: number; maxWidth?: Length; minHeight?: number; maxHeight?: Length; alignment?: Alignment };
    background?: Color;
    cornerRadius?: number;
    opacity?: number;
    foreground?: Color;
    widgetAccentable?: boolean;
    privacySensitive?: boolean;
  }
  interface Container extends Modifiers { children?: Child }

  export function Widget(props: Container & { url?: string; background?: Color; relevance?: number }): WidgetNode;
  export function VStack(props: Container & { align?: "leading" | "center" | "trailing"; spacing?: number }): WidgetNode;
  export function HStack(props: Container & { align?: "top" | "center" | "bottom"; spacing?: number }): WidgetNode;
  export function ZStack(props: Container & { align?: Alignment }): WidgetNode;
  export function Grid(props: Container & { hSpacing?: number; vSpacing?: number; align?: Alignment }): WidgetNode;
  export function GridRow(props: Container): WidgetNode;
  export function Text(props: Modifiers & { font?: Font; color?: Color; weight?: "regular" | "medium" | "semibold" | "bold" | "heavy"; design?: "default" | "rounded" | "monospaced" | "serif"; lineLimit?: number; minScale?: number; align?: "leading" | "center" | "trailing"; children?: Child }): WidgetNode;
  export function Image(props: Modifiers & { src?: string; symbol?: string; resizable?: boolean; aspect?: "fit" | "fill"; color?: Color; font?: Font }): WidgetNode;
  /** A date that updates live without a refresh. Note: importing it as `Date` shadows the global Date in that file; prefer DateText. */
  export function Date(props: Modifiers & { value: globalThis.Date | string | number; style?: "relative" | "timer" | "time" | "date" | "offset"; font?: Font; color?: Color }): WidgetNode;
  export const DateText: typeof Date;
  export function Gauge(props: Modifiers & { value: number; range?: [number, number]; label?: string; style?: "linear" | "circular"; color?: Color }): WidgetNode;
  export function ProgressView(props: Modifiers & { value: number; total?: number; label?: string; color?: Color }): WidgetNode;
  export function Chart(props: Modifiers & { data: Record<string, JSONValue>[]; mark?: "line" | "bar" | "area" | "point"; x: string; y: string; color?: Color }): WidgetNode;
  /** Runs an exported script function in the widget extension, then reloads the widget. */
  export function Button(props: Modifiers & { intent: IntentFunction; params?: Record<string, JSONValue>; symbol?: string; label?: string; children?: Child }): WidgetNode;
  /** `isOn` comes from the script, so it survives reloads; iOS shows the new state while the intent runs. */
  export function Toggle(props: Modifiers & { isOn: boolean; intent: IntentFunction; params?: Record<string, JSONValue>; label?: string; symbol?: string; children?: Child }): WidgetNode;
  export function Link(props: Container & { url: string }): WidgetNode;
  export function Spacer(props?: Modifiers & { minLength?: number }): WidgetNode;
  export function Divider(props?: Modifiers): WidgetNode;
}

```

# Complete example: Daylight

```tsx
import type { WidgetContext } from "kite";
import { Widget, VStack, HStack, Text, Image, Spacer, ProgressView, DateText } from "kite/ui";

export const config = defineScript({
  name: "Daylight",
  description: "A quiet daily dashboard with a countdown to midnight. No network needed.",
  icon: { symbol: "sun.horizon.fill", color: "#72DCC5" },
  widget: { families: ["small", "medium", "large"], refresh: "hourly" },
});

function card(ctx: WidgetContext, date: Date) {
  const days = ["Sunday", "Monday", "Tuesday", "Wednesday", "Thursday", "Friday", "Saturday"];
  const months = ["Jan", "Feb", "Mar", "Apr", "May", "Jun", "Jul", "Aug", "Sep", "Oct", "Nov", "Dec"];
  const start = new Date(date); start.setHours(0, 0, 0, 0);
  const end = new Date(start); end.setDate(end.getDate() + 1);
  const progress = (date.getTime() - start.getTime()) / (end.getTime() - start.getTime());
  const small = ctx.family === "small";
  return (
    <Widget background="#0D1C2C">
      <VStack align="leading" spacing={small ? 7 : 10} frame={{ maxWidth: "infinity", maxHeight: "infinity", alignment: "leading" }}>
        <HStack spacing={6}>
          <Image symbol="sun.horizon.fill" font="caption" color="#72DCC5" />
          <Text font="caption2" weight="semibold" color="#72DCC5">{days[date.getDay()].toUpperCase()}</Text>
          <Spacer minLength={0} />
          {!small && <Text font="caption2" color="#A5B9CA">A LITTLE ROOM FOR GOOD THINGS</Text>}
        </HStack>
        <HStack align="center" spacing={12}>
          <Text font="largeTitle" weight="heavy" design="rounded" color="#FFFFFF" lineLimit={1} minScale={0.6}>
            {months[date.getMonth()]} {date.getDate()}
          </Text>
          {!small && <Spacer minLength={0} />}
          {!small && <VStack align="trailing" spacing={3}>
            <Text font="caption2" color="#A5B9CA">LEFT TODAY</Text>
            <DateText value={end} style="timer" font="title2" color="#FFFFFF" />
          </VStack>}
        </HStack>
        <Spacer minLength={0} />
        {ctx.family === "large" && <VStack align="leading" spacing={8} padding={16} background="#172D40" cornerRadius={18} frame={{ maxWidth: "infinity", alignment: "leading" }}>
          <Text font="title2" weight="semibold" color="#FFFFFF">One small thing.</Text>
          <Text font="body" color="#BED0DE">Choose something that would make today feel well spent.</Text>
        </VStack>}
        <ProgressView value={progress} color="#72DCC5" />
        <Text font="caption2" color="#A5B9CA">{Math.floor(progress * 100)}% of today · make the rest yours</Text>
      </VStack>
    </Widget>
  );
}

export function widget(ctx: WidgetContext) {
  const now = new Date(ctx.date);
  // Fifteen-minute dated entries update the progress value without JS polling.
  // The native timer counts down live; iOS still controls timeline scheduling.
  return Array.from({ length: 9 }, (_, index) => {
    const date = new Date(now.getTime() + index * 15 * 60 * 1000);
    return { date, view: card(ctx, date) };
  });
}

```

# Complete example: Focus Session

```tsx
import { storage } from "kite";
import type { WidgetContext, Control } from "kite";
import { Widget, VStack, HStack, Text, Image, Button, Spacer, DateText } from "kite/ui";

export const config = defineScript({
  name: "Focus Session",
  description: "A 25-minute focus timer. Start/stop from the widget or start from Control Center.",
  icon: { symbol: "moon.stars.fill", color: "#C4B5FD" },
  widget: { families: ["small", "medium", "large", "accessoryRectangular"], refresh: "hourly" },
});

export async function startFocus() {
  await storage.set("focusEnd", Date.now() + 25 * 60 * 1000);
  return { reload: true };
}
export async function stopFocus() {
  await storage.remove("focusEnd");
  return { reload: true };
}

function card(ctx: WidgetContext, end: number, active: boolean) {
  const lock = ctx.family === "accessoryRectangular";
  if (lock) return <Widget><VStack align="leading" spacing={2}>
    <Text font="headline">{active ? "Focus in progress" : "Room to focus"}</Text>
    {active ? <DateText value={new Date(end)} style="timer" font="title3" /> : <Text font="caption">Start a session from Control Center.</Text>}
  </VStack></Widget>;
  return <Widget background="#1B1530"><VStack align="leading" spacing={8} frame={{ maxWidth: "infinity", maxHeight: "infinity", alignment: "leading" }}>
    <HStack spacing={6}>
      <Image symbol="moon.stars.fill" font="caption" color="#C4B5FD" />
      <Text font="caption2" weight="bold" color="#C4B5FD">FOCUS SESSION</Text>
      <Spacer minLength={0} />
    </HStack>
    {active ? <DateText value={new Date(end)} style="timer" font="largeTitle" color="#FFFFFF" /> : <Text font="largeTitle" weight="heavy" design="rounded" color="#FFFFFF">25:00</Text>}
    <Text font="caption" color="#C4B5FD">{active ? "One thing at a time." : "Make room for one thing."}</Text>
    <Spacer minLength={0} />
    {ctx.family === "large" && <Text font="title2" weight="semibold" color="#FFFFFF">A small pocket of undivided attention.</Text>}
    <Button intent={active ? stopFocus : startFocus} symbol={active ? "stop.circle" : "play.circle.fill"} label={active ? "Stop" : ctx.family === "small" ? "Start" : "Start 25 min"} foreground="#C4B5FD" />
  </VStack></Widget>;
}

export async function widget(ctx: WidgetContext) {
  const saved = await storage.get<number>("focusEnd");
  const end = typeof saved === "number" && Number.isFinite(saved) ? saved : 0;
  const now = new Date(ctx.date);
  const active = end > now.getTime();
  const current = { date: now, view: card(ctx, end, active) };
  // The second entry ends the countdown display when the session finishes.
  return active ? [current, { date: new Date(end), view: card(ctx, end, false) }] : [current];
}

export const control: Control = {
  kind: "button", title: "Start focus", symbol: "moon.stars.fill",
  async press() { return startFocus(); },
};
export async function run() {
  console.log("Use Start in the preview/widget, or add Kite Button → Focus Session in Control Center.");
}

```

# Complete example: Quiet Frame

```tsx
import { http } from "kite";
import type { WidgetContext } from "kite";
import { Widget, ZStack, VStack, Text, Image } from "kite/ui";

export const config = defineScript({
  name: "Quiet Frame",
  description: "A landscape photo card. Uses Kite's native image downscaling and a one-day cache.",
  icon: { symbol: "photo.on.rectangle.angled", color: "#B1DAC6" },
  widget: { families: ["small", "medium", "large"], refresh: "hourly" },
  settings: { caption: { type: "text", title: "Caption", default: "Take the scenic route." } },
  permissions: ["network"],
});

export async function widget(ctx: WidgetContext) {
  const width = Math.max(80, (ctx.displaySize?.width || 338) - 32);
  const height = Math.max(80, (ctx.displaySize?.height || 158) - 32);
  try {
    // Use http.image, rather than putting the remote URL directly into <Image>.
    // Kite downloads and downsizes it natively for the current widget dimensions.
    const photo = await http.image("https://picsum.photos/id/10/1200/900", { cache: "1d" });
    return <Widget background="#10251E">
      <ZStack align="bottomLeading" frame={{ width, height }} cornerRadius={18}>
        <Image src={photo} resizable aspect="fill" frame={{ width, height }} />
        <VStack align="leading" spacing={3} padding={10} background="#10251E" opacity={0.94} frame={{ maxWidth: "infinity", alignment: "leading" }}>
          <Text font="caption2" weight="bold" color="#B1DAC6">PAUSE &amp; LOOK</Text>
          <Text font="headline" color="#FFFFFF" lineLimit={1} minScale={0.7}>{String(ctx.settings.caption || "Take the scenic route.")}</Text>
        </VStack>
      </ZStack>
    </Widget>;
  } catch (error) {
    console.warn("Quiet Frame:", String(error));
    return <Widget background="#10251E"><VStack spacing={8}>
      <Image symbol="photo" font="largeTitle" color="#B1DAC6" />
      <Text font="headline" color="#FFFFFF">A quiet moment.</Text>
      <Text font="caption" color="#B1DAC6">Run in Kite with internet access to load the photo.</Text>
    </VStack></Widget>;
  }
}

```

# Complete example: Water Garden

```tsx
import { storage } from "kite";
import type { WidgetContext } from "kite";
import { Widget, VStack, HStack, Text, Image, Button, Spacer, ProgressView } from "kite/ui";

export const config = defineScript({
  name: "Water Garden",
  description: "A daily counter with + and undo buttons. The goal is yours to choose.",
  icon: { symbol: "drop.fill", color: "#17866B" },
  widget: { families: ["small", "medium", "large"], refresh: "hourly" },
  settings: { goal: { type: "number", title: "Daily goal", default: 8, min: 1, max: 24 } },
});

function today() {
  const d = new Date();
  return `water-${d.getFullYear()}-${d.getMonth() + 1}-${d.getDate()}`;
}
function count(value: unknown): number {
  const n = Number(value);
  return Number.isFinite(n) ? Math.max(0, Math.min(99, Math.floor(n))) : 0;
}
export async function addGlass() {
  await storage.update<number>(today(), value => Math.min(99, count(value) + 1));
  return { reload: true };
}
export async function undoGlass() {
  await storage.update<number>(today(), value => Math.max(0, count(value) - 1));
  return { reload: true };
}

export async function widget(ctx: WidgetContext) {
  const glasses = count(await storage.get<number>(today()));
  const goal = Math.max(1, Math.min(24, count(ctx.settings.goal ?? 8)));
  const small = ctx.family === "small";
  return (
    <Widget background="#EDF7EF">
      <VStack align="leading" spacing={small ? 5 : 9} frame={{ maxWidth: "infinity", maxHeight: "infinity", alignment: "leading" }}>
        <HStack spacing={5}>
          <Image symbol="drop.fill" font="caption" color="#17866B" />
          <Text font="caption2" weight="bold" color="#17866B">WATER GARDEN</Text>
          <Spacer minLength={0} />
          {!small && <Text font="caption2" color="#527365">FRESH START, EVERY DAY</Text>}
        </HStack>
        <HStack align="center" spacing={6}>
          <Text font="largeTitle" weight="heavy" design="rounded" color="#153E31">{glasses}</Text>
          <Text font="title3" color="#527365">/ {goal}</Text>
          <Spacer minLength={0} />
          {!small && <Image symbol="leaf.circle.fill" font="largeTitle" color="#17866B" />}
        </HStack>
        {ctx.family === "large" && <HStack spacing={6}>
          {Array.from({ length: Math.min(goal, 10) }, (_, i) => <Image key={i} symbol={i < glasses ? "drop.fill" : "drop"} font="title3" color={i < glasses ? "#17866B" : "#A9C5B5"} />)}
        </HStack>}
        <ProgressView value={Math.min(glasses, goal)} total={goal} color="#17866B" />
        <Text font="caption2" color="#527365">{glasses >= goal ? "Your goal is complete." : "A little, often."}</Text>
        <Spacer minLength={0} />
        <HStack spacing={12}>
          <Button intent={undoGlass} symbol="minus.circle" label={small ? "" : "Undo"} foreground="#527365" />
          <Spacer minLength={0} />
          <Button intent={addGlass} symbol="plus.circle.fill" label={small ? "" : "Add"} foreground="#17866B" />
        </HStack>
      </VStack>
    </Widget>
  );
}

export async function run() {
  console.log(`${count(await storage.get<number>(today()))} glasses recorded today. Use the preview or widget buttons to change it.`);
}

```
